Astro Hunters
Hunting beyond the obvious. Exploring forgotten equipment, decoding its stories, and turning remnants of space exploration into discoveries for the future.
summary: For Challenge No. 1, Astro Hunters created a streamlined tool using open-source NASA data. Our solution transforms complex space metrics into simple, interactive visuals for researchers and the public.
details:
ASTRO HUNTER – Chasing the Unknown Beyond Earth

Project Description

ASTRO HUNTER is an interactive educational and space-exploration platform designed to uncover the fascinating stories of human-made hardware left behind during space missions. From lunar landers and rover components to scientific instruments on distant planetary surfaces, our project explores the forgotten technological footprints of humanity beyond Earth.

1. What does it do and how does it work?

ASTRO HUNTER transforms information about space hardware into an engaging digital exploration experience. Users can explore different planetary locations, discover objects left behind by space missions, and learn about their origins, scientific purposes and historical significance.

The platform is designed to include:

  • An interactive Solar System exploration map.
  • A database of 30–50 space hardware objects.
  • Mission-based storytelling explaining the history behind each object.
  • A 3D gallery for exploring space equipment.
  • Interactive quizzes to test scientific knowledge.
  • Detailed information about the missions, locations and purposes of the equipment.

2. What are its benefits?

ASTRO HUNTER makes complex space science accessible, interesting and interactive. Instead of simply reading about space missions, users can explore their history through visual storytelling and digital experiences.

Its major benefits include:

  • Promoting awareness of humanity's space exploration history.
  • Encouraging curiosity about astronomy, engineering and technology.
  • Making scientific information accessible to students and space enthusiasts.
  • Highlighting the importance of understanding human-made objects left beyond Earth.
  • Supporting STEM education through interactive learning.

3. What is the intended impact?

Our vision is to transform the way people understand the history of space exploration.

ASTRO HUNTER aims to inspire young learners to look beyond Earth, appreciate scientific achievements and think critically about the future of space exploration.

It also encourages awareness of responsible space exploration, including the importance of monitoring space debris and considering the long-term environmental and operational consequences of space missions.

Our ultimate goal is to turn forgotten space hardware into valuable learning opportunities for the next generation of explorers.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware or software were used?

The project uses a web-based development approach.

Our planned and developing technology stack includes:

  • HTML5: To structure the website and its content.
  • CSS3: To create the visual design and responsive layouts.
  • JavaScript: To develop interactive features and user experiences.
  • GitHub and GitHub Pages: For source-code management, version control and website hosting.
  • NASA Open APIs and NASA Image and Video Library: To access publicly available mission information and authentic space imagery.
  • NASA Planetary Data System: As a scientific information resource.
  • 3D visualisation tools and libraries: For presenting planetary environments and space hardware interactively.

The project is primarily software-based and does not require physical hardware.

5. How is the project creative and innovative?

ASTRO HUNTER approaches space exploration from a different perspective. Most educational platforms focus on successful launches, discoveries and active missions. Our project focuses on another fascinating aspect: the objects humanity has left behind while exploring the unknown.

We combine scientific information, interactive mapping, storytelling, 3D visualisation and gamified learning to create an experience that makes space history feel like an adventure.

Our central creative idea is simple:

Every abandoned machine has a story. Every location holds a piece of history. Every discovery opens a new question.

6. What factors did our team consider?

While developing ASTRO HUNTER, we considered:

  • Scientific accuracy: Using reliable information from NASA and other recognised space agencies.
  • Accessibility: Making the platform understandable for students and general audiences.
  • User engagement: Creating an interactive rather than purely informational experience.
  • Authenticity: Distinguishing actual mission records and photographs from conceptual illustrations.
  • Educational value: Connecting space exploration with STEM learning.
  • Technical feasibility: Selecting accessible web technologies and publicly available datasets.
  • Responsible exploration: Raising awareness about space debris, mission hardware and sustainable space exploration.

Our Vision

ASTRO HUNTER is more than a digital catalogue of abandoned space equipment. It is an invitation to explore the untold stories of humanity's journey beyond Earth.

We don't just chase discoveries in space; we chase the stories that those discoveries leave behind.
